Case_06008/figure1.jpg.source_caption: Gram stain of ascitic fluid (primary cytospin).

description.short_caption: Gram stain of ascitic fluid showing gram-negative bacilli and inflammatory cells.
description.detailed_description: This image shows a Gram stain of ascitic fluid prepared via cytospin technique. Numerous gram-negative bacilli are visible, appearing as pink, rod-shaped organisms. There are also large, round inflammatory cells (likely neutrophils) present, indicating an inflammatory response. The background is relatively clear, consistent with a cytospin preparation.
visible_findings: clear background typical of cytospin preparation

Case_06008/figure2.jpg.source_caption: Gram stain of culture of aspirate, from blood bottle.

description.short_caption: Gram stain showing gram-positive bacilli from a culture aspirate.
description.detailed_description: This image shows a Gram stain of a culture aspirate, likely from a blood culture bottle. Numerous gram-positive bacilli are visible, appearing as pink to red rod-shaped organisms against a lighter background. The organisms are scattered throughout the field, with some clustering noted. No other cell types, such as white blood cells, are prominently visible in this field.

Case_06008/figure4.jpg.source_caption: Gram stain of growth from blood agar plate.

description.short_caption: Gram stain showing gram-positive cocci in chains.
description.detailed_description: This image shows a Gram stain with numerous gram-positive cocci arranged in chains. The organisms are stained purple, consistent with their gram-positive nature, and are distributed across the field in a chain-like pattern. The background is clear, suggesting this is a pure culture, likely obtained from a growth on a blood agar plate. The morphology is characteristic of streptococcal species.

Case_06008/figure3.jpg.source_caption: Gram stain of culture of aspirate, from blood bottle.

description.short_caption: Gram stain showing Gram-positive rods and cocci from a culture aspirate.
description.detailed_description: This image shows a Gram stain of a culture aspirate. Multiple Gram-positive rods and cocci are visible, appearing as pink to red structures against a lighter background. The rods are arranged singly and in chains, while the cocci are seen in clusters. The staining technique highlights the morphology and Gram reaction of the organisms.
visible_findings: Pink to red staining of organisms
Light background typical of Gram stain
